messages.content: "Could you please provide me with the historical dividend data for Microsoft for the past 5 years on a quarterly basis, then the same data but on an annual basis? After that, could you retrieve the stock market data for Microsoft for the past 60 days and then for the past 120 days?"

function.name: corporate_finance_dividend_data
function.description: Get historical dividend data of a specific company within a particular duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

company.description: The company that you want to get the dividend data for.

years.description: Number of past years for which to retrieve the data.

frequency.description: The frequency of the dividend payment.

function.name: stock_market_data
function.description: Retrieve stock market data for a specific company and time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

company.description: The company that you want to get the stock market data for.

days.description: Number of past days for which to retrieve the data.

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

1) Historical dividend data for Microsoft (MSFT) for the past 5 years on a quarterly basis.

2) Same data but on an annual basis.

3) Stock market data for MSFT for the past 60 days.

4) Then for the past 120 days.

We have two available tool calls: corporate_finance_dividend_data and stock_market_data. We need to call them accordingly.

First we should fetch dividend data for Microsoft for last 5 years at quarterly frequency. That means we will pass company="Microsoft" or maybe ticker symbol "MSFT". Usually the API expects company name; let's use "Microsoft".

Second, again for annual frequency.

Third, stock market data for Microsoft for 60 days.

Fourth, stock market data for Microsoft for 120 days.

We'll produce separate outputs for each request. We'll do four tool calls sequentially.

But note: The system says "When calling a tool, only give the arguments required." So we just supply JSON objects as per signature.

Also after retrieving results from tool calls, we can output them directly. But we might also combine into one response. However guidelines say if multiple requests, respond separately. In this case it's all part of single query though. It's okay to return combined answer.

Let's proceed step-by-step.

Call first tool: corporate_finance_dividend_data(company:"Microsoft", years:5, frequency:"quarterly").

Then second tool: corporate_finance_dividend_data(company:"Microsoft", years:5, frequency:"annual") - Wait they said "past 5 years" so still 5 years.

Third: stock_market_data(company:"Microsoft", days:60).

Fourth: stock_market_data(company:"Microsoft", days:120).

Return responses.

Ok. Let's make sure not to include extraneous text when calling tools. Just JSON object.

Proceed.
